description.narrative: Insatsen syftar till att bidra till att adressera IGAD:s institutionella brister, vilka hindrar IGAD från att leverera effektivt på sitt mandat kopplat till pelarna i IGAD:s regionala strategi (2021 - 2025). Det övergripande målet för det strategiska partnerskapet kring ISAP IV:s är att stärka IGAD:s organisatoriska förmåga samt den operationella effektiviteten och bygga upp ett sammanhängande och stärkt samarbete mellan IGAD och intressenter (medlemsstater, givare, privata sektorn, civilsamhällesorganisationer och andra) för ökad transparens och ansvarsskyldighet, såväl som effektiv leverans av tjänster. Genuskvalitet är målinriktat genom detta program, det syftar till att ta itu med befintliga klyftor när det gäller tillämpningen av genusanalys i utformningen av program och införlivande av genuskänsliga indikatorer i IGAD:s övervaknings- och utvärderingsramverk. IGAD planerar också att göra en uthållig opinionsbildning och lobbyverksamhet bland medlemsstaterna för att minska ojämlikhetsklyftan och möta kvinnors och barns prioriteringar och specifika behov. Främjande av jämställdhet och empowerment för kvinnor är således ett av de sju tematiska områden som programmet syftar till att leverera. Det geografiska område som täcks är Afrikas Horn (Djibouti, Etiopien, Kenya, Somalia, Sydsudan, Sudan och Uganda).

The programme aims to contribute to address the key institutional performance gaps still hampering IGAD from delivering its mandate in an effective and efficient manner through the pillars of IGAD’s Regional Strategy (2021-2025). The overall objective of the strategic partnership of ISAP IV is to reinforce IGAD’s corporate performance and operational efficiency and build a coherent and collaborative engagement between IGAD and stakeholders (Member States, development partners, private sector, civil society organizations and others) for increased transparency and accountability, as well as effective delivery of services. Gender quality is targeted through this programme, it aims to address existing gap in terms of the application of gender analysis in the design of programmes and incorporation of gender sensitive indicators in IGAD's monitoring and evaluation frameworks. IGAD also plans to make sustained advocacy and lobbying among the Member States to narrow the inequality gap and meet the priorities and specific needs of women and children. Thus, Promoting Gender Equality and Women Empowerment is one of the seven thematic areas the program aims to deliver. The targeted geographical area is the Horn of Africa (Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda).

The overall objective of ISAP IV is: To reinforce IGADs corporate performance and operational efficiency and build a coherent and collaborative engagement between IGAD and stakeholders for increased transparency and accountability. The objective of ISAP IV contributes to the attainment of the strategic development objective of the Corporate Development Services Pillar of the IGAD regional strategyfor 2021-25, which is to contribute to transforming IGAD through enhancing its institutional capacity to effectively and efficiently deliver its mandate. Phase four of ISAP comprises two expected outcomes: (1) Corporate performance and operational efficiency of IGAD (Secretariat and Specialised Institutions) enhanced, and (2) Collaborative engagement between IGAD (Secretariat and Specialised Institutions) and stakeholders (Member states, development partners, private sector, civil society organizations and others) for effective delivery of services and obligations established.

description.narrative:
- The ratification process of the IGAD Treaty is progressing at different stages across Member States. Ethiopia, Djibouti, and South Sudan have fully ratified the treaty, while Kenya and Somalia have secured executive approval and are advancing toward parliamentary endorsement. Sudan and Eritrea are working towards the ratification process, with ongoing consultations expected to determine their timelines. Uganda has adopted but not yet signed the treaty, pending further national deliberations. The treaty will officially come into force once Kenya and Somalia complete their ratification processes.
- IGAD Vision 2050: IGAD held an executive consultative and validation of the Vision 2050. The goal of Vision 2050 is to transform IGAD into a resilient, peaceful, prosperous, and integrated region mirroring the upper middle-income region where citizens enjoy a high quality of life by 2050. Vision 2050 consultants were held in-depth consultations with all the Member States (except Eritrea and Sudan). In addition, the Member States also participated in the executive consultation and validation of the Vision 2050.
- IGAD developed the IGAD Centralized statistics database management system for the IGAD region. The database will be finalized and launched in the fourth quarter of the year. This database, once operational, will serve as a robust repository for statistical data collected from Member States. It will provide a central platform for data sharing, analysis, and dissemination, significantly enhancing data accessibility and promoting evidence-based decision-making within the region.
- Mid-term review (MTR) of the Regional Strategy 2021-2025: the MTR was held during the period, and it revealed significant progress achieved, institutional reforms and initiatives that had been implemented to transform IGAD into an efficient organization, including strengthening internal controls, institutional policy development, enhancement of business processes. The MTR also noted a need to improve the implementation progress of the strategy through more coordinated planning and implementation, adequate funding, communication, and visibility and monitoring and evaluation system. The MTR will also help IGAD prepare for the subsequent strategy (2026-2030).
- Assessed Member States contribution formula: IGAD completed the report on the Member States assessed contribution formula. The report, which was the result of a detailed study, provides a new formula aimed at better aligning member states' contributions with their respective economic capacities. Following the completion of the study, IGAD conducted national consultations with member states to review the proposed formula and consensus reached with them. These consultations allowed for an in-depth discussion with stakeholders, and IGAD received valuable inputs and feedback from the member states. The feedback provided will be considered for refining the formula to ensure it addresses the concerns and economic realities of all IGAD members. This marks an important step in strengthening the financial sustainability of IGAD while promoting fairness and transparency in member state contributions.
